substantial.problem: The 1778 turn to Rome is stated as settled and as the patriarch's act. On 29 April 1778 Patriarch Elia died; on 30 April it was his nephew Hormizd, a metropolitan and not patriarch, who embraced Rome. His cousin Yeshua-yau was agreed as patriarch and recanted in May 1779. Rome let Hormizd act as patriarch only without the seal (1782). Labourt dates his definite union to 1830 (excommunicated 1818). The Josephite see had an administrator to 1826 (Labourt), its last holder dying 1828 (Wigram). 'In 1778 the patriarch of the plain turned to Rome' (why, teaser, longDescription) and 'By 1815 ... The line of the plain had joined Rome' (legacy) are wrong or overstated, and the dated sources disagree (Wigram 1778 vs Labourt 1830), so the claim is contested and needs both sides. The VIII.40 link note ('the patriarch of the plain submitted ... His nephew Hormizd was reconciled ... in 1830') makes the patriarch and the nephew two different converts.
substantial.evidence: Badger v1 lines 8040-8065 ("made me Metropolitan"; uncle died 29 April; "I and Yeshua-yau were reconciled ... It was moreover agreed that he should be Patriarch in the room of my uncle; but a few months had hardly elapsed when he again became a heretic ... May, 1779"); lines 8100-8104 (licence "but I was not allowed to use the patriarchal seal", Pius VI, A.D. 1782). Labourt raw (own fetch): "Joseph (V) Augustine Hindi succeeded (1779-1826) ... Administrator"; "John Hormizd had been excommunicated in 1818, but was reconciled with Rome in 1830"; "went over definitely to the Catholic Church (1830)". Wigram lines 7498-7502: "in 1778, the Elia line in Mosul made a final and definite submission ... the 'Joseph' line at Diarbekr was allowed to lapse— though the last holder of it did not die till 1828".
substantial.fix: why: "The Church of the East had two patriarchs in 1650, one in the mountains and one on the plain. In 1681 the pope named a third, at Diyarbakır. In 1778 the patriarch of the plain died of plague, and the next day his nephew Hormizd turned to Rome. He wrote down the date: 30 April." teaser: "... An ancient church with three patriarchs at once. In 1778 the patriarch's nephew turned to Rome." longDescription[4]: "In 1778 the line of the plain began to turn to Rome. Patriarch Elia died of plague at Alqosh on 29 April. His nephew Hormizd, a metropolitan, wrote the next part himself, in Badger's English: “So on the 30th of April I embraced all that the holy Church believes.” His cousin Yeshua-yau was to be patriarch. Within a year he turned back, and the two became enemies. In 1782 Pope Pius VI let Hormizd act as patriarch, but not use the patriarch's seal. The sources disagree on when the plain line truly joined Rome. Wigram puts it in 1778. Labourt puts it in 1830, after Hormizd had been cut off by Rome in 1818. Wigram says the Joseph line was then allowed to lapse, though its last holder lived until 1828." (Score it; split if FRE < 60.) legacy: "By 1815 the church stood divided. On the plain, Hormizd led a party in union with Rome, but Rome had not yet made him patriarch. The line of the mountains stayed outside Rome's obedience. Its later story is told in the entry on the Church of the East and the Chaldean Consolidation." Link note: "In 1778 Hormizd, nephew of the dying patriarch of the plain, turned to Rome. Labourt writes that he was cut off in 1818, reconciled in 1830 and named patriarch of Babylon. The line of the mountains stayed outside." Add fact-table rows for each new sentence (Badger 8059-8063 Yeshua-yau; 8100-8104 Pius VI 1782; Labourt 1818/1830; Wigram 7500-7502 for 1828).
